source: Rating Roulette: Self-Inconsistency in LLM-As-A-Judge Frameworks
finding: Same model, same prompt, repeated runs gives different judgments. This is occasion noise in Kahneman's terms. Self-agreement is low on subjective tasks.
numbers: Krippendorff alpha over 3 runs, SummaC: Llama-3.1-70B 0.326, DeepSeek-R1-Distill 0.628, Qwen3-32B 0.788. MT-Bench: 0.265, 0.507, 0.563. No model reached 0.8 on MT-Bench. Qwen3 gave same MT-Bench judgment on all 3 runs in only 61.3% of cases. Sampling temperature 0.6.
quote: gave the same judgment on all 3 runs for only 61.3% of cases
limits: Open-weight models only; no GPT-5 or Claude tested; human labels also noisy.
agent_relevance: Judging a candidate once is a noisy act. The scaffold should treat any single LLM verdict as one draw, and should have code, not the model, aggregate.

source: Rating Roulette: majority vote of 3 runs and sampling off
finding: Majority vote of 3 runs beats the average single run for every model. Turning sampling off lowers accuracy and does not remove the problem.
numbers: SummaC balanced accuracy, single run mean / majority of 3 / no sampling: Llama 59.1 / 61.4 / 58.4; DeepSeek 69.8 / 72.3 / 69.3; Qwen3 79.4 / 80.6 / 79.2. Single-run SD 0.32 to 2.06 points. 5 or 10 runs gave no significant change vs 3.
limits: Gain is small (1 to 2.5 points). Greedy decoding was worse here than sampling plus vote.
agent_relevance: Cheap noise reduction: 3 independent judgments combined by code. More than 3 gave little extra on this task. Greedy decoding is not the fix.

source: Rating Roulette: prompts do not fix self-reliability
finding: Few-shot examples and chain-of-thought did not raise self-agreement. More reasoning did not make judgments more repeatable.
numbers: Few-shot (5 pos, 5 neg): alpha change under 0.01 per model; accuracy Llama 62.9, DeepSeek 72.8, Qwen 80.6. CoT: alpha fell slightly; accuracy 60.8, 71.6, 80.4. Both: 60.1, 72.1, 80.3 (vs single-run 59.1, 69.8, 79.4).
limits: SummaC binary task only for this ablation; 3 open models.
agent_relevance: Adding thinking steps does not cut noise by itself. Variance reduction needs sampling plus aggregation (G4 style), not a longer prompt.

source: Rating Roulette: LLM judges versus human agreement
finding: On MT-Bench human-human agreement is itself modest. Best LLM judge nearly matches humans on accuracy, but all are noisy.
numbers: Accuracy / alpha: human-human 0.827 / 0.478; GPT-4 0.671 / 0.396; Llama 0.556 / 0.239; DeepSeek 0.668 / 0.385; Qwen3 0.719 / 0.426. SummEval expert-expert alpha: consistency 0.798, fluency 0.588, relevance 0.398; crowd-crowd 0.48 to 0.51; best LLM-expert 0.726 (consistency); fluency low or negative.
limits: Human labels are a noisy gold standard too.
agent_relevance: Judge noise differs by criterion: factual consistency is stable, fluency and relevance are not. Use LLM verdicts mostly where criteria are crisp.

source: Lau (2026) Same Input, Different Scores: inconsistency of LLM judge
finding: Five models score identical RAG answers differently on repeated runs, even at temperature 0. Completeness is the noisiest criterion; relevance the steadiest.
numbers: Models: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Claude Haiku 4.5, Claude Sonnet 4.5; temp 0 and 1; 10 runs per question; scores 0 to 1 on relevance, accuracy, completeness. No model fully deterministic.
limits: Private enterprise dataset, size not stated in the text I extracted; results read mostly from figures; one prompt.
agent_relevance: Level noise (strict vs generous judge) and occasion noise both show up. Pin a rubric and run multiple samples.

source: Lau (2026): cross-model strictness and temperature effects
finding: Model families differ in strictness: Gemini most generous on completeness. Temperature 0 cuts spread for GPT and Gemini (Gemini near zero) but little for Claude models, sometimes more variance.
numbers: SD of scores over 10 runs; Gemini SD near 0 at temp 0; Claude Haiku/Sonnet marginal change; Claude Haiku completeness SD higher at temp 0 than temp 1. Mean scores similar across temperatures.
limits: Qualitative reading of heatmaps; one prompt; top-p and seed untested.
agent_relevance: Judge-to-judge disagreement is a level-noise term. Mixing model families as judges averages out strictness bias; one fixed judge bakes it in.

source: Schroeder and Wood-Doughty (2025) Can You Trust LLM Judgments? Reliability of LLM-as-a-Judge
finding: A single LLM judgment is one sample. Inter-rater reliability across seeds swings widely. They propose McDonald's omega over many samples as a reliability measure.
numbers: Seed test on BBH, 3 judges, temp 0.25, 100 judgments each: inter-rater reliability ranged 0.167 to 1.000 across seeds. Judges: Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Starling-LM-7B-beta, Gemma-1.1-7b-it; five temperatures 0 to 1; Head-to-Tail replication omega about 0.99.
limits: Small 7-8B judges; temperature effect goes both ways by model and task.
agent_relevance: Reliability ranking of judges inverted their Chatbot Arena ranking, so a higher-scoring model may be a noisier judge. Measure the judge's own reliability before trusting it.

source: Atil et al. (2025) Non-Determinism of Deterministic LLM Settings
finding: With temperature 0 and fixed settings, outputs and accuracy still vary between identical runs. Cause is likely compute-level (batching, buffers).
numbers: 5 LLMs, 8 tasks, 10 runs, zero-shot and few-shot: accuracy varies up to 15% across runs; best-to-worst gap up to 70%; no LLM repeatable across all tasks. Metrics TARr@N (raw) and TARa@N (parsed answers).
quote: We see accuracy variations up to 15% across naturally occurring runs.
limits: Abstract page only read; exact models not in abstract.
agent_relevance: Pure system noise cannot be removed by setting temperature 0; measure it by repeating runs.

source: Sclar et al. (2024) Quantifying Language Models' Sensitivity to Spurious Features in Prompt Design
finding: Meaning-preserving prompt format changes shift accuracy hugely. Scale, more shots and instruction tuning do not remove it.
numbers: Spread of up to 76 accuracy points with LLaMA-2-13B across formats; good formats correlate only weakly across models. FormatSpread estimates the range without weights.
quote: performance differences of up to 76 accuracy points
limits: Abstract page only read.
agent_relevance: Report and average over several prompt phrasings; a single wording is a hidden noise source. Use paraphrased prompts across samples.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Large Language Models are not Fair Evaluators
finding: Swapping the order of two answers can flip the LLM judge's winner. Order is an irrelevant factor producing noise.
numbers: Vicuna-13B beats ChatGPT on 66 of 80 queries with ChatGPT as evaluator when order is manipulated. Fixes: multiple evidence, balanced position (average over both orders), human-in-the-loop via diversity entropy.
quote: Vicuna-13B could beat ChatGPT on 66 over 80 tested queries
limits: Abstract page only read; no numeric gain recorded.
agent_relevance: Always judge pairs in both orders and combine in code. Cheap and general.

source: Shi et al. (2024) Judging the Judges: position bias in LLM-as-a-judge
finding: Position bias is not random chance, varies by judge and task, and is stronger when the quality gap between candidates is small.
numbers: 15 judges, 22 tasks (MTBench, DevBench), about 40 answer-generating models, over 150,000 evaluation instances. Metrics: repetition stability, position consistency, preference fairness.
quote: position bias is not due to random chance
limits: Abstract page only read.
agent_relevance: Close calls are where noise matters most, so flag near-ties for extra samples rather than a flat sample count.

source: Zheng et al. (2023) Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
finding: GPT-4 judge agrees with human preferences over 80%, about the level of human-human agreement, but shows position, verbosity and self-enhancement bias.
numbers: Over 80% agreement; 3K expert votes; 30K conversations.
limits: Abstract page only read; agreement is on pairwise preferences, not scores.
agent_relevance: Prefer pairwise comparison with order swap over absolute scores when possible.

source: Stureborg et al. (2024) Large Language Models are Inconsistent and Biased Evaluators
finding: LLM evaluators prefer low-perplexity text, produce skewed rating distributions, anchor in multi-attribute ratings, and agree poorly across samples.
numbers: SummEval and RoSE datasets. No numbers in abstract.
limits: Abstract page only read.
agent_relevance: Anchoring in multi-attribute scoring is the halo effect from the noise book: score each criterion in a separate call.

source: Zheng et al. (2024) Large Language Models Are Not Robust Multiple Choice Selectors
finding: Answers change when option order changes. Cause is mainly a token prior for labels like A. PriDe estimates the prior by permuting a few samples and debiases the rest.
numbers: 20 LLMs, 3 benchmarks, ICLR 2024 Spotlight.
quote: modern LLMs are vulnerable to option position changes in MCQs due to their inherent 'selection bias'
limits: Abstract page only read; no accuracy gain numbers read.
agent_relevance: Shuffle choices across samples. Order is pure noise, so averaging over permutations cancels it.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning
finding: Sample many reasoning paths and take the most common answer. It is the direct 'average many judges' fix for LLM noise.
numbers: Gains over greedy CoT: GSM8K +17.9, SVAMP +11.0, AQuA +12.2, StrategyQA +6.4, ARC-challenge +3.9 points.
quote: self-consistency boosts the performance of chain-of-thought prompting with a striking margin
limits: Needs an extractable answer; sample count not read; gains smaller on commonsense tasks.
agent_relevance: Core of the schema's selection step: code takes the plurality, not the model's own pick.

source: Li et al. (2024) More Agents Is All You Need
finding: Plain sampling and voting improves with more instances, and the gain depends on task difficulty. It stacks with other methods.
numbers: No numbers on the abstract page.
limits: Abstract page only read.
agent_relevance: Compute spent on independent samples plus a vote scales; spend more on hard items.

source: Chen et al. (2023) Universal Self-Consistency
finding: For free-form outputs, the LLM picks the sample most consistent with the others. Matches standard self-consistency on math and execution-based voting on code.
numbers: On par with self-consistency on math; matches execution-based voting on code without execution. No figures read.
quote: USC effectively utilizes multiple samples and improves the performance
limits: Abstract page only read. Uses the model as selector, so selector noise returns.
agent_relevance: When answers cannot be string-matched, selection is again a judgment and again noisy. Prefer code-checkable answers.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Mixture-of-Agents Enhances LLM Capabilities
finding: Layers of different LLMs refine each other's answers. Mixing model families beats a single strong model.
numbers: AlpacaEval 2.0 LC win rate 65.1% for open-source-only MoA vs 57.5% for GPT-4 Omni.
quote: MoA models achieves state-of-art performance on AlpacaEval 2.0, MT-Bench and FLASK, surpassing GPT-4 Omni.
limits: Abstract page only read; judged by an LLM with its own biases.
agent_relevance: Diverse judges give less correlated errors, the independence condition in the noise book.

source: Schoenegger et al. (2024) Wisdom of the Silicon Crowd
finding: An ensemble of 12 LLMs forecasts about as well as a human crowd. Averaging cancels noise. Models show acquiescence above 50%.
numbers: 31 binary questions, 925 human forecasters, 3-month tournament. LLM crowd not statistically different from human crowd. Study 2: showing the human median improved GPT-4 and Claude 2 by 17 to 28%; human+machine average better still.
quote: the LLM crowd outperforms a simple no-information benchmark and is not statistically different from the human crowd
limits: Small question set; 2023 models; abstract page only read.
agent_relevance: A crowd of different models is the wisdom-of-crowds remedy for noise; correct known bias (yes-lean) after averaging.

source: Halawi et al. (2024) Approaching Human-Level Forecasting with Language Models
finding: Retrieval-augmented LM system with ensemble aggregation nears the crowd aggregate of competitive forecasters, sometimes beats it.
numbers: No Brier scores or N read from the abstract page.
quote: On average, the system nears the crowd aggregate of competitive forecasters
limits: Abstract page only read.
agent_relevance: Retrieval plus aggregation of several forecasts is a ready pattern for a noise-reduced estimate step.

source: Kahneman, Sibony, Sunstein (2021) Noise: A Flaw in Human Judgment
finding: Defines system noise = level noise (judge average differs) + pattern noise (judge x case) + occasion noise. Not opened this session; figures recalled, not verified.
numbers: Recalled, unverified: insurance underwriters' premium quotes differed by about 55% median where executives expected 10%.
limits: Not opened; verify against the book before use.
agent_relevance: Frames what to measure in an LLM: repeat the same case (occasion), vary the judge or prompt (level, pattern).

source: Noise book: decision hygiene and mediating assessments protocol
finding: Remedies: aggregate independent judgments, structure into independent sub-judgments, delay holistic intuition, use rules and checklists. Recalled, not opened.
numbers: None verified.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Maps to: independent samples, per-criterion calls, code-held aggregate, hold final intuition until evidence is scored.

source: Kleinberg et al. (2018) Human Decisions and Machine Predictions
finding: Algorithm trained on bail data beat judges and had no judge-to-judge noise. Recalled, not opened.
numbers: Recalled, unverified: crime cut up to 24.7% at same jail rate, or jailing cut 41.9% at same crime.
limits: Not opened; selective labels problem.
agent_relevance: A fixed rule is noise-free but needs data; a code-held rule inside the loop plays that role.

source: Practitioner heuristic: judge self-agreement under 85% is unreliable
finding: Blog says stochastic judges are used as deterministic oracles; suggests pinning snapshots, median of samples, 85% self-agreement cutoff. Seen in a search snippet only.
numbers: 85% threshold is informal vendor advice.
limits: Not opened; not peer reviewed.
agent_relevance: Treat as a practical alarm threshold, not evidence.
